title: Oscillopathic features and neuromodulation with tACS in people with Parkinson’s disease: A semi-systematic review
title_zh: 帕金森病患者的振荡异常特征与经颅交流电刺激（tACS）神经调制：半系统综述
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is associated with prominent changes in neural oscillatory activity. These occur at cortical and subcortical sites, strongly predict clinical deficit, and are normalised by therapy. Interventions targeting oscillatory activity therefore represent an avenue for novel clinical approaches in people with PD. Transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) holds substantial appeal in this endeavour. This non-invasive brain stimulation (NIBS) technique can induce functionally and clinically relevant changes in oscillatory activity. Furthermore, it has not been associated with any serious adverse effects, is portable and relatively cheap. A growing number of studies have therefore investigated applications of tACS in PD and the aim of this review was to provide an overview of this literature. Of particular focus was identifying how recent advances within the neuromodulation space - across conceptual, physiological and methodological domains - might inform next generation applications of tACS. Review of the existing literature reveals several studies that have reported beneficial effects of tACS on symptomatology and neurophysiological deficit in people with PD. Furthermore, preliminary trials using multi-session dosing report long-lasting effects, supporting the clinical utility of a tACS based therapy. In addition, work in animal models provides important characterisation of neurobiological mechanisms contributing to beneficial effects of tACS, highlighting neuroprotective processes involving neurotrophins. Together, this literature demonstrates the potential benefits of tACS in people with PD. However, further development in future work stands to increase the impact and application of this technique, with examination of novel neurophysiological features, greater individualisation and optimised targeting being prominent areas on interest.
abstract_zh: 帕金森病（PD）与显著的神经振荡活动变化相关。这些变化发生在皮层和皮层下部位，强烈预测临床缺陷，并可通过治疗得到正常化。因此，针对振荡活动的干预代表了对PD患者新型临床方法的一个途径。经颅交流电刺激（tACS）在此领域具有巨大吸引力。该非侵入性脑刺激（NIBS）技术能够诱导功能性和临床相关的振荡活动变化，并且未与任何严重不良反应相关，且便携且相对廉价。越来越多的研究已探讨tACS在PD中的应用，本综述的目标是概述该文献。特别关注的是识别神经调制领域——在概念、生理和方法学层面——的最新进展如何为下一代tACS应用提供信息。对现有文献的回顾显示，已有若干研究报告tACS对PD患者症状和神经生理缺陷的有益影响。此外，使用多次剂量的初步试验报告了持久效果，支持基于tACS的治疗的临床实用性。动物模型研究进一步阐明了tACS产生益处的神经生物学机制，强调了涉及神经营养因子的神经保护过程。综上所述，这些文献展示了tACS在PD患者中的潜在益处。然而，未来工作中的进一步发展有望提升该技术的影响力和应用范围，重点关注新颖的神经生理特征、更高的个体化和优化的靶向策略。
